subject: Game Theory
title: Voter Turnout Puzzle
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Voter Turnout Puzzle.

hook.text: Your single vote almost never decides an election. Rationally, the cost of voting exceeds the expected benefit.

buildup.text: Yet millions vote. This is the 'paradox of voting'—rational self-interest predicts nobody should bother.

discovery.text: People vote for expressive reasons: duty, identity, and the desire to feel part of a collective decision.

twist.text: If everyone reasoned this way and stayed home, a single voter would become decisive—making voting worthwhile again.

climax.text: Compulsory voting (Australia, Belgium) solves the turnout problem by eliminating the individual choice not to vote.

punchline.text: Voting is rational in ways math misses.

quiz.question: What is the paradox of voting?
options: Individual cost of voting exceeds the expected impact
